standard.title: Control of Air Pollution in Cement Plants — Code of Practice (First Revision)
standard.sector: Environment Pollution / Environmental Protection and Waste Management
standard.description: This standard covers the identification of air pollutants from the cement industry, their sources, dust control equipment (design and selection), and stack height, monitoring, and maintenance guidelines to systematically manage and abate atmospheric emissions.
standard.scope: This standard covers the identification of air pollutants from the cement industry, their sources, dust control equipment (design and selection), and stack height, monitoring, and maintenance guidelines to systematically manage and abate atmospheric emissions.

version.current_version: First Revision, May 2025 (developed from draft Doc No. EED 02 (24202))

amendments.summary: No active amendments have been issued on this newly established 2025 revision (NIL on this copy).

certification.description: Voluntary Code of Practice. Since IS 12002:2025 is an engineering code of practice and guideline rather than a direct consumer product, it does not carry a mandatory BIS 'ISI Mark' product stamp. However, compliance with its structural designs, duct velocities, in-built scrubbers, and stack heights is legally enforced across India by the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) and State Pollution Control Boards (SPCBs) under the statutory mandates of MoEF&CC notifications G.S.R. 496 (E) and G.S.R. 497 (E) to authorize a plant's Consent to Operate (CTO).
requirements: Identifies that the massive volumes of alkaline cement dust emitted by these facilities (ranging from 5 to 250 micrometers) represent the primary atmospheric pollution hazard, and the code acts as a design manual to select appropriate dust control equipment (such as ESPs, baghouses, cyclones, and scrubbers) to minimize surrounding habitat exposure.

Requires optimizing raw milling operations so that the raw mill can be operated to act as an in-built SO2 abatement system for the kiln. Flue gases from the preheater kiln are routed directly through the raw mill, where the highly alkaline raw materials dry, grind, and absorb SO2.

Specifies that sulphur introduced through fuels fed to preheater kilns will not lead to significant SO2 emissions because of the strong alkaline environment inside the sintering zone, the calcination zone, and the lower stage of the preheater, ensuring this sulphur is safely captured and locked in the clinker.

Mandates maintaining an excess oxygen level of 1 percent to 3 percent O2 in the kiln flue gases. This concentration is critical to ensure satisfactory clinker and cement product quality while minimizing incomplete combustion products like carbon monoxide (CO).

Specifies that cement plants utilizing co-processing (feeding hazardous or non-hazardous wastes into cement kilns for energy and material recovery) must strictly satisfy and comply with the emission norms notified by MoEF&CC vide notification G.S.R. 497 (E).
Specifies that standard cement plants must satisfy and comply with the emission norms notified by MoEF&CC vide notification G.S.R. 496 (E).

Any observed or calculated test or analysis value expressing emission concentrations, moisture content, temperatures, or volume must be mathematically rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 2022. The number of significant places retained must be identical to the specified value in the standard.
